themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints have spiked to 8 this week versus a baseline of 1.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 392% increase (z-score: 9.16)—suggesting either an acute public health hazard, pest infestation, or animal welfare breakdown requiring immediate investigation and cleanup coordination.
evidence: 8 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (392% spike, z-score: 9.16)
Highest statistical anomaly in dataset by z-score, indicating unprecedented departure from norm
Timing suggests acute trigger rather than chronic condition
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks and Sanitation on response protocols and whether a specific outbreak (rats, wildlife) is driving complaints
Canvass affected blocks to determine if complaints cluster geographically and what residents observed

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 22 two weeks ago versus a 2.8 weekly baseline—a 700% spike (z-score: 7.74)—indicating a potential coordinated tagging campaign or breakdown in enforcement that warrants investigation of which corridors are most affected and whether gang activity is involved.
evidence: 22 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 7.74)
Second-highest z-score in dataset, indicating major anomaly
Aligns with community concern about street conditions and neighborhood quality of life
reporting_angles: Map where the 22 complaints originated to identify whether tagging is concentrated on a specific corridor (e.g., Flatbush Ave near transit hub)
Interview Parks Dept on enforcement response and timeline for remediation

themes_detail.label: Parking Enforcement Pullback
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints dropped 80% to 33 this week from a baseline of 166.8 per week—a statistically significant decline (z-score: -3.91)—suggesting either a policy shift, enforcement absence, or data anomaly that should be verified with NYPD and DOT.
evidence: 33 illegal parking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 166.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (80% decline, z-score: -3.91)
Inverse signal: notable drop rather than spike, but statistically anomalous and warrants explanation
Could indicate enforcement pause related to ongoing Flatbush Avenue bus redesign (per Gothamist, 2026-04-09)
reporting_angles: Confirm with NYPD and DOT whether enforcement has been reduced in advance of Flatbush Avenue transit project
Ask whether 311 reporting itself has declined (data quality issue) or actual violations have decreased

themes_detail.label: Water System Strain
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints surged to 39 three weeks ago versus a baseline of 9.5 per week—a 310% spike (z-score: 5.6)—pointing to potential infrastructure failure, main break, or pressure issues that may be linked to broader plumbing failures (630 complaints over 90 days, highest single category).
evidence: 39 water system complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 9.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (310% spike, z-score: 5.6)
Plumbing category highest overall 90-day volume at 630 complaints, plus 454 water leak complaints
Heat/hot water also tops list at 3,781 complaints over 90 days, suggesting systemic building infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Interview DEP on whether a main break or pressure loss was recorded 3 weeks ago in CD 309
Cross-reference with plumbing and water leak complaints to determine if spike has subsided or is ongoing

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints reached 3 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—warranting DOHMH investigation into whether a specific establishment or food source triggered multiple incidents in Flatbush.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Matches graffiti spike timing (both 2 weeks ago), suggesting possible event-driven trigger or data artifact
DOHMH should have inspection records and closure data linked to complaints
reporting_angles: Request DOHMH inspection reports and violations for the 2-week period to identify specific establishments cited
Interview DOHMH on whether complaints point to common source (e.g., restaurant, food vendor) or distributed incidents
